newsitem.title: USA: Whitewater's McDougals get mixed news.
newsitem.headline: Whitewater's McDougals get mixed news.

text.p: - James and Susan McDougal, President Clinton's former Whitewater business partners who are both in jail, got mixed news Tuesday from the federal courts.

James McDougal's petition to be freed while appealing his conviction for fraud was denied, while his former wife, Susan McDougal, was granted a hearing on her motion to be released from jail for failing to cooperate with the Whitewater investigation.

Clinton and his wife were partners with the McDougals in an Arkansas real estate project called Whitewater when he was governor during the 1970s. The project failed, as did a savings and loan business owned by McDougal.
Prosecutors are attempting to determine whether money from the savings and loan was improperly diverted to Whitewater.

A federal appeals court upheld a district judge and refused James McDougal's petition to be released from prison while his appeal is considered. McDougal, 56, entered a federal prison hospital June 16 to begin serving a three-year sentence for fraud and conspiracy.
The appeals court said McDougal "has not met his burden" of demonstrating that his conviction would likely be overturned or a new trial granted.

Also Tuesday, a federal district judge at Little Rock scheduled a hearing for Friday morning to hear arguments in an petition by Susan McDougal to be set free from her contempt of court citation. She had been jailed since September, 1996 for refusing to answer questions about Clinton from by prosecutors probing the personal and political finances of the Clintons.
McDougal was convicted in the same trial in which James McDougal was found guilty. Clinton was a witness for the defence.

McDougal has said that prosecutors asked her if Clinton had testified truthfully when he said he had no knowledge of an illegal loan she had received. McDougal said she knew of no criminal behaviour by either of the Clintons but feared she would be indicted for perjury unless her answers pleased the prosecutors.

In a letter filed with the court Tuesday, Susan McDougal's attorney, Michael Kennedy of New York, said his client had demonstrated, by "enduring nine months of hell in three jails" that she would not cooperate with the Whitewater prosecutors.
